prompt.v: An ellipse has center (−1, −1), a vertex at (−1, −11) and a focus at (−1, 7). Which is its equation?

problems.explain: The vertices are 10 from the center, above or below it, so a = 10 and a² = 100 goes under y. The foci are 8 from it, so c = 8, and for an ellipse b² = a² − c² = 100 − 64 = 36. So (x + 1)²/36 + (y + 1)²/100 = 1. The others: (x + 1)²/164 + (y + 1)²/100 = 1 takes b² = a² + c², adding where an ellipse takes away; (x + 1)²/100 + (y + 1)²/36 = 1 puts a² under x; (x + 1)²/100 + (y + 1)²/164 = 1 does both.

So x²/64 + y²/100 = 1. The others: x²/136 + y²/100 = 1 takes b² = a² + c², adding where an ellipse takes away; x²/100 + y²/64 = 1 puts a² under x; x²/100 + y²/136 = 1 does both.

So (y − 2)²/36 − (x + 4)²/64 = 1. The others: (y − 2)²/36 − (x + 4)²/136 = 1 takes b² = c² + a², adding where a hyperbola takes away; (x + 4)²/36 − (y − 2)²/64 = 1 puts a² under x; (x + 4)²/36 − (y − 2)²/136 = 1 does both.

So (y − 4)²/64 − x²/36 = 1. The others: (y − 4)²/64 − x²/164 = 1 takes b² = c² + a², adding where a hyperbola takes away; x²/64 − (y − 4)²/36 = 1 puts a² under x; x²/64 − (y − 4)²/164 = 1 does both.

The foci are 13 from it, so c = 13, and for a hyperbola b² = c² − a² = 169 − 25 = 144. So (y − 1)²/25 − (x − 3)²/144 = 1. The others: (y − 1)²/25 − (x − 3)²/194 = 1 takes b² = c² + a², adding where a hyperbola takes away; (x − 3)²/25 − (y − 1)²/144 = 1 puts a² under x; (x − 3)²/25 − (y − 1)²/194 = 1 does both.
